# Separation loses exactly the relation

<!-- Generated by build_result_registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

> Describing the parts separately gives back the whole exactly where it is rectangular; a relation forms only by joint action, lasts under separate laws that lose nothing, and ends only by loss or joint action; parity is a whole its pairs do not give back.

<a id="主张-claim"></a>
## Claim

Let whole be a whole on A × B (which combinations occur). It is rectangular (Rectangular) when whole (a, b) and whole (a′, b′) give whole (a, b′); the separated description (Separated whole p) says only that each part of p occurs. Separation keeps every combination that occurs (separated_of_whole), and it contains only what occurs exactly when whole is rectangular (separation_faithful_iff); two parts that always go alike can go apart when described separately (separation_admits_extra). Three parts can be related as a whole while every two are free: in the even-parity triples any two values complete to an even triple, and (true, false, false) is not one (whole_not_in_pairs); on Specker's three boxes and three pairs (restrict, Glued and PartsDetermine of Becoming.Context) every reading is allowed by every pair (evenBoxes_glued) and the pairs do not give the whole back (evenBoxes_not_determined). Write imageOf next whole for the configurations a law next leads to from whole. A law moving each part by itself (f × g) keeps a whole rectangular, lossy or not (Rectangular.image_of_separate); the law copying the first part into the second turns the full whole into the parts being equal, which is not rectangular (copy_relates). Where f merges no two first parts that occur and g no two second parts, a rectangular image under f × g gives a rectangular whole (Rectangular.of_image_injective), so a whole that is not rectangular stays so under such a law (relation_persists). A law sending the first part to one value, however it moves the second, leads to a rectangular whole (forgetting_unrelates). For example, couple (x, y) = (x, flipIf x y) on Bool × Bool is an involution (couple_couple); it leads from “the second part is false” (rectangular) to a whole that is not rectangular, and acting again back to “the second part is false” (coupling_relates_and_unrelates). No Lean axiom is used.

Canonical source: [Description.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Description.lean)

<a id="前提与对应-hypotheses-and-correspondence"></a>
## Hypotheses and correspondence

- No premise: separation_faithful_iff is two-way and holds for every whole; Rectangular.image_of_separate holds for any f and g.
- relation_persists needs f and g to merge nothing that occurs (a local condition, written into the theorem).
- For the witnesses: parity, copying and couple are on Bool.

The first part of P70 (work board), following Ren's “push the frontier, as far as possible” of 12 October 2026, answering Ren's “the framing may lose something” and “what makes a pair, a pair?”: what describing the parts separately deducts is exactly the relation; “what can go together” is the record at a moment of “how they go on”. Readings (the AI's, adopted on Ren's delegation; Ren agreed with the reply containing them): a correlation is the memory of a meeting; 三生万物 read as three being the least number at which a whole holds a relation no part holds. The other way parts fail a whole (parts allowing what no whole has) is no_whole of contextual-registration, on the same three pairs. See §94 of the integration note.

Relation is stated for wholes of two parts, with parity as the witness for three; which joint laws keep wholes rectangular is not characterized; a coupling ending a relation has one witness; PartsDetermine and separation_faithful_iff are not related as instance and law (the two parts have different types); the readings are the AI's; contains no ethical predicate.

- A whole that is not rectangular gains combinations when described separately (separation_admits_extra); the even parity of three parts is held by no pair (whole_not_in_pairs); a lossless coupling can end a relation (coupling_relates_and_unrelates), so losing nothing does not keep a relation without “moving each part by itself”. ## Dependencies and related results

- **formal-reuse**: [contextual-registration](contextual-registration.md). Reuses restrict, Glued, PartsDetermine and Specker's boxes and pairs: on the same three pairs parity is a whole its pairs do not give back.

**Output:** What a whole allows within a context, what the parts glue to, whether the parts give the whole back; three boxes and three pairs.

**Input:** Parity as the witness of the first way parts fail a whole.

**Preserved conditions:** None. [Context.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Context.lean)

- Related, not a proved adapter: [the-split-that-makes-sense](the-split-that-makes-sense.md). Same module: the split that makes sense, relative to the map; here, what any description cutting a whole into parts loses.
- Related, not a proved adapter: [projection-carrying-a-law](projection-carrying-a-law.md). A projection carries a law exactly where what it lumps goes alike; here laws moving each part by itself keep wholes rectangular, and joint laws can relate or unrelate the parts.
- Related, not a proved adapter: [gluing-under-parity](gluing-under-parity.md). The exact law for the same kind of case of parts failing a whole: for parity constraints, context-free readings exist exactly where no selection of contexts contradicts.
